class BytesIOCopy(io.BytesIO):
    """Patch ``io.BytesIO`` to let the written stream be copied to another.

    .. versionadded:: 8.2
    """

    def __init__(self, copy_to: io.BytesIO) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.copy_to = copy_to

    def flush(self) -> None:
        super().flush()
        self.copy_to.flush()

    def write(self, b: ReadableBuffer) -> int:
        self.copy_to.write(b)
        return super().write(b)

    def fileno(self) -> int:
        """Raise the same error a real pipe-less stream would.

        ``io.BytesIO`` normally raises this already, but some callers
        (e.g. code invoking ``subprocess.run(..., stdout=sys.stdout)``)
        check ``hasattr(stream, "fileno")`` first. Since this class does
        define ``fileno``, make sure it still fails the same way rather
        than returning a bogus value, so callers get a clear error
        instead of writing to the wrong place.

        See: https://github.com/pallets/click/issues/2647
        """
        raise io.UnsupportedOperation(
            "The stream captured by CliRunner has no real file descriptor. "
            "Passing it to APIs like subprocess.run(stdout=...) is not "
            "supported."
        )

class BytesIOCopy(io.BytesIO):
    """Patch ``io.BytesIO`` to let the written stream be copied to another.

    .. versionadded:: 8.2
    """

    def __init__(self, copy_to: io.BytesIO) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.copy_to = copy_to

    def flush(self) -> None:
        super().flush()
        self.copy_to.flush()

    def write(self, b: ReadableBuffer) -> int:
        self.copy_to.write(b)
        return super().write(b)

    def fileno(self) -> int:
        """Back this stream with a real file so callers that need an
        actual file descriptor (e.g. ``subprocess.run(stdout=...)``)
        keep working instead of raising ``io.UnsupportedOperation``.

        The current contents are copied into a temporary file the
        first time this is called, and the object starts proxying
        further reads/writes to it so everything stays consistent.

        See: https://github.com/pallets/click/issues/2647
        """
        self._real_file = tempfile.TemporaryFile()
        self._real_file.write(self.getvalue())
        self._real_file.seek(self.tell())
        return self._real_file.fileno()

        super().flush()
        self.copy_to.flush()

    def write(self, b: ReadableBuffer) -> int:
        self.copy_to.write(b)
        return super().write(b)

    def fileno(self) -> int:
        """Back this stream with a real file so callers that need an
        actual file descriptor (e.g. ``subprocess.run(stdout=...)``)
        keep working instead of raising ``io.UnsupportedOperation``.

        The current contents are copied into a temporary file the
        first time this is called, and the object starts proxying
        further reads/writes to it so everything stays consistent.

        See: https://github.com/pallets/click/issues/2647
        """
        self._real_file = tempfile.TemporaryFile()
        self._real_file.write(self.getvalue())
        self._real_file.seek(self.tell())
